descriptors.concept_name: Penal Consequences For Failure To Deduct Or Collect Or Pay Tax At Source
descriptors.definition: Statutory penalties and rigorous imprisonment are attracted when a person fails to deduct tax at source, collect tax at source, or remit such withheld amounts to the credit of the Central Government. These provisions apply equivalently whether the underlying consideration is monetary or delivered in kind under specific statutory provisions.
inclusion: Penalty equal to un-deducted tax under section 271C
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay deducted tax under section 276B
Penalty equal to un-collected tax under section 271CA
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay collected tax under section 276BB
Penalties for failure to pay or ensure payment when consideration is in kind under relevant provisos
exclusion: Prosecution under section 276B if payment is made to the credit of the Central Government on or before the prescribed statement filing time w.e.f. 1.10.2024
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between civil monetary penalties levied by the Joint Commissioner and criminal prosecution involving rigorous imprisonment.
Distinguishes between defaults relating to tax deduction at source versus tax collection at source.
